originalTitle: ‘It is British life’: No 10 vows to stop councils trying to limit standing in pubs
summary: Westminster council has recommended banning ‘vertical drinking’ or ordering at the bar in new draft licensing policy
content: No 10 has vowed to confiscate powers from local councils which try to restrict customers from standing up while drinking in pubs or ordering at the bar. It comes after the Guardian revealed on Thursday that Westminster council in central London recommended not allowing “vertical drinking” or ordering at the bar in its new draft licensing policy. The draft document, now out for consultation, recommends that pubs applying for new licences allow only table service rather than bar ordering. It also suggests new pubs in popular nightlife areas including Soho call last orders at 10pm, to reduce noise and disturbance. A Downing Street spokesperson said: “Busy pubs full of people talking to each other is not a public nuisance, it is British life, and it is thousands of jobs. “The government is devolving new licensing powers to the mayor [of London] to help support pubs and nightlife. Soho did not become world famous by taking last orders early, switching the lights off at 10 o’clock. “The prime minister encourages local leaders to work with the industry so that pubs can continue to thrive.” The government is due to grant new powers to the London mayor, Sadiq Khan, allowing him to “call in” local council decisions he opposes. Khan said of the proposals on X: “You can’t run a world-famous nightlife district with a village-hall mindset.” A spokesperson for the mayor previously said he was against “restrictive and anti-growth policies” and said he hoped to use new powers to be granted to him by the government to stop councils from overreaching. The draft policy says pubs should “discourage excessive drunkenness and encourage the provision of more seating in premises that serve alcohol for people to sit and enjoy a drink and order food by table service in place of open bar space that caters for high-volume vertical drinking”. It goes on to recommend that sales of alcohol and food should be “by waiter or waitress service only”. Operators of pubs and bars in Soho have criticised what they see as overly restrictive licensing policies and said the proposals could kill off West End nightlife. Paul Swaddle, the Conservative leader of Westminster council, denied the plans amounted to a ban on “vertical drinking”. He told the Press Association that newspapers had carried “confusing stories” about the document and added: “I want to be straight with people. There is no plan, and never has been, to ban drinking while standing up in a Westminster pub.” Responding to Khan’s criticism, he said: “We don’t need lectures from city hall on backing hospitality when they have directed the police to object to every new licence application as their solution to curbing crime in the West End.” The council also plans to ban the opening of new pubs and bars in what it terms the “cumulative impact zone”, encompassing Soho and large parts of the West End. Areas such as Victoria and Mayfair will also face restrictions on new openings if the draft policy is made official.
chineseTitle: “这就是英国人的生活”：10人誓言阻止议会试图限制酒吧里的地位
chineseSummary: 威斯敏斯特议会建议在新的许可政策草案中禁止“垂直饮酒”或在酒吧点餐
chineseContent: No 10 发誓要没收地方议会的权力，这些议会试图限制顾客在酒吧喝酒或在酒吧点餐时站起来。此前《卫报》周四透露，伦敦市中心的威斯敏斯特议会建议在其新的许可政策草案中不允许“垂直饮酒”或在酒吧点餐。目前正在征求意见的文件草案建议申请新许可证的酒吧只允许餐桌服务而不是酒吧点餐。它还建议苏豪区等热门夜生活区的新酒吧在晚上 10 点进行最后点餐，以减少噪音和干扰。唐宁街的一位发言人表示：“繁忙的酒吧里挤满了人们互相交谈，这并不是公害，而是英国人的生活，而且是数以千计的就业机会。”政府正在向伦敦市长下放新的许可权力，以帮助支持酒吧和夜生活。 Soho 并没有因为提早接受最后订单、在 10 点关灯而闻名于世。 “总理鼓励当地领导人与该行业合作，以便酒吧能够继续蓬勃发展。”政府将授予伦敦市长萨迪克·汗新的权力，允许他“呼吁”他反对的地方议会决定。 Khan 谈到 X 的提议时表示：“你不能以村会所的心态来经营世界著名的夜生活区。”市长发言人此前表示，他反对“限制性和反增长政策”，并表示希望利用政府授予他的新权力来阻止议会过度扩张。该政策草案称，酒吧应“阻止过度饮酒，并鼓励在提供酒类的场所提供更多座位，供人们坐下来享用饮料并通过餐桌服务点餐，以代替开放的酒吧空间”。
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于全球新闻信号，适合用于观察外部环境、政策变化、地缘风险和市场情绪。
